indexLevelObservations.observation: THREE unrelated 'C-number' / 'RC' namespaces coexist in this corpus: (a) RC-C0..RC-C11 reconstruction chapters, (b) RIC-C1..RIC-F1 Rich Content implementation stages, (c) RC1..RC9 refresh-continuity root causes. A fourth near-collision exists in the C2 Follow adjudication rulings R1-R10 versus the C1 accepted-exception labels R1/R2. Every one of these appears as a bare token in at least one governed document.

TWO certification vocabularies coexist without reconciliation: the RC layer table (Architecture / Implementation / Product-Behavior / Cross-System / Real-Boundary / Founder Acceptance / Item 17) and the §12 validation classes (LOCALLY VERIFIED / AUTHORIZED-BROWSER VERIFIED / TWO-ACCOUNT-TWO-BROWSER / LIVE_CERTIFIED). Finding states use the second vocabulary; chapter states use the first.

The doctrines that govern the 2026-08-16..18 work (Conversation canon, Invitation canon, §12 Rich Content, Live Origination Correction) each declare their own boundaries and each name RC-C4 as Attention owner — so they consistently RESPECT the RC frame at its edges while operating outside its sequencing. No governed document states whether they are inside, alongside, or superseding the RC roadmap.

Findings discipline is asserted independently in three places and must not be relaxed by any later stage: F126 and F138 must not be merged (§12 line 35); F131 and F139-F142 intersect but must not be merged (Amendment 1 §E); F064/F113 remain separate rows with an explicit duplication note and F050 ⊂ F053 ⊂ F116 plus F059-F070 ⊂ F117 are recorded as hierarchy, not compression (transcript register).
